description: README documentation and CLI tests. Depends on FEAT-001 being complete (tests import from src/cli.ts and src/mcp.ts). Creates the package README with quick-start, configuration, and architecture sections, plus unit tests for CLI argument parsing.
steps: 1. Create README.md at project root. Structure: (A) Title: '# warden-mcp' with one-line description: 'MCP security gateway that scans every tool call for prompt injection attacks'. (B) 'Quick Start' section: install with `bun add -g warden-mcp` or `npm i -g warden-mcp`. Kiro config example in `.kiro/settings/mcp.json`: `{ "mcpServers": { "warden": { "command": "bunx", "args": ["warden-mcp", "--upstream-cmd", "uvx mcp-server-fetch"], "env": { "OPENAI_API_KEY": "sk-..." } } } }`. Claude Desktop config example in `claude_desktop_config.json`: `{ "mcpServers": { "warden": { "command": "bunx", "args": ["warden-mcp", "--config", "/path/to/.warden.json"], "env": { "OPENAI_API_KEY": "sk-..." } } } }`. (C) 'What It Does' paragraph: Warden sits between AI host and upstream MCP servers, scanning every tool description and tool result through a multi-stage detection pipeline (rules, classifier, similarity, LLM judge) before content reaches the AI model. Blocked content is replaced with a safe message. (D) 'Configuration' section: table of env vars (OPENAI_API_KEY, WARDEN_FAIL_MODE, JUDGE_MODE, JUDGE_MODEL, CLASSIFIER_THRESHOLD, SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD) and .warden.json format showing upstreams, policy, and judge blocks. (E) 'CLI Flags' section listing all flags from cli.ts --help. (F) 'Architecture' section: brief paragraph on the 7-stage pipeline (extract → decode → rules → classifier → similarity → judge → session). (G) 'Without a Judge LLM' section: works without OPENAI_API_KEY — rules, classifier (Prompt Guard 2), and similarity stages still run; only the LLM judge stage is skipped. No API key needed for basic protection. (H) 'Development' section: `bun run dev` for API server, `bun run test` for tests, `bun run eval` for evaluation suite.

2. Create tests/cli.test.ts: Use `import { describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test'`. Test cases: (A) '--help flag prints usage': spawn `bun src/cli.ts --help` as a subprocess using `Bun.spawn`, capture stderr, verify it contains 'warden-mcp' and 'Usage', verify exit code 0, verify stdout is empty. (B) 'unknown flag shows error': spawn with `--unknown-flag`, verify exit code is non-zero. (C) '--api-only starts HTTP server': spawn `bun src/cli.ts --api-only --port 0`, wait 2s for startup, read the port from stderr output (the log line prints it), fetch GET http://localhost:<port>/metrics, verify 200 response, kill the process. (D) 'arg parsing collects multiple --upstream-cmd': this tests the parsing logic directly — import the arg parser function from cli.ts (or test via subprocess with multiple --upstream-cmd flags and --help to verify they're accepted). Use `afterEach` or `afterAll` to clean up spawned processes.
acceptance_criteria: README.md exists at project root with Quick Start, What It Does, Configuration, CLI Flags, Architecture, Without a Judge LLM, and Development sections
README includes working Kiro config example with bunx warden-mcp
README includes working Claude Desktop config example
tests/cli.test.ts exists and passes: DB_PATH=./warden-test.db bun test tests/cli.test.ts
All existing tests still pass: DB_PATH=./warden-test.db bun test
findings: README.md created with all required sections (Quick Start, What It Does, Configuration, CLI Flags, Architecture, Without a Judge LLM, Development). Kiro and Claude Desktop config examples included. 4 CLI tests added: --help output, unknown flag rejection, --api-only HTTP server startup with /metrics health check, multiple --upstream-cmd acceptance. All 320 tests pass (316 existing + 4 new).
